note: Pakistan's largest banks are HBL, National Bank, UBL, MCB and Meezan; HBL and UBL, among the largest card issuers, are written; the others weren't reached in this pass. Both schedules are before federal excise duty and provincial sales tax, whose rates they don't state, and the tax isn't written. HBL's schedule of bank charges (1 July to 31 December 2026, read again 2026-10-30): service charges at most 42% a year on the amount outstanding, written at that figure, and on cash advances 42% a year; the annual fee 6,500 rupees for the HBL Green Card (this file's card since 2026-10-29), 14,000 for Gold, 22,000 for Platinum; the Fuel Saver cards a monthly fee instead, 350 rupees (Green) or 700 (Gold); a cash advance 1,200 rupees or 3%, whichever is higher; a late fee of 2,500 rupees a month; spending in another currency 4%; a returned cheque 1,200 rupees. UBL's schedule of charges (July to December 2026, effective 1 July 2026, read 2026-10-30): the Visa primary card's annual fee 6,000 rupees (Classic), 12,000 (Gold), 22,000 (Platinum); 44% a year on purchases and cash advances; a cash advance 1,200 rupees or 3%, whichever is higher; a late payment 2,200 rupees; spending abroad 4.5% or 100 rupees, whichever is higher (written as 4.5%); over the limit 1,600 rupees; a returned cheque 1,000 rupees. The Visa Signature and the Mastercards, kept for former Silkbank customers, aren't written. Neither schedule states a minimum payment or grace period.
